glossary: Agrément
Formal approval by the receiving state of a proposed ambassador, given before appointment.
Persona non grata
A diplomat declared unacceptable by the host state, who must then be recalled or dismissed.
Démarche
A formal representation made by one government to another to convey a position or protest.
Letters of Credence
Documents by which an ambassador is accredited to the head of state of the receiving country.
High Commission
The embassy-equivalent between Commonwealth countries, headed by a High Commissioner.
Consulate
An office in a city abroad for visas, passports, trade and citizen services; not the main diplomatic mission.
Chargé d'affaires
Diplomat who temporarily heads a mission when the ambassador is absent.
Diplomatic immunity
Protection of diplomats from the host country's jurisdiction, codified in the Vienna Convention 1961.
Diplomatic bag
Sealed bag carrying official correspondence, protected from search or seizure.
Extradition
Surrender of an accused or convicted person by one state to another for trial or punishment.
Note verbale
A formal, unsigned diplomatic note written in the third person.
Aide-mémoire
Informal written summary of a position handed over during a diplomatic meeting.
Joint communiqué
Official statement issued after talks, summarising what the parties agreed.
MoU
Memorandum of Understanding: a record of intent, usually not legally binding, unlike a treaty.
Track-II diplomacy
Unofficial dialogue between non-government experts, academics or former officials.
Soft power
Joseph Nye's term for influence through culture, values and attraction rather than force.
Apostille
A certificate under the 1961 Hague Convention that makes a public document valid in member countries; India is a member.
Panchsheel
Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence, from the 1954 India–China agreement.
Gujral Doctrine
I. K. Gujral's 1996–97 policy of non-reciprocal goodwill towards India's smaller neighbours.
Act East Policy
India's engagement with Southeast and East Asia, upgraded from Look East in 2014.
Neighbourhood First
India's policy of priority to relations with immediate neighbours.
Strategic autonomy
Independence in foreign-policy choices without formal alliance with any bloc.
Bilateral / Multilateral
Between two states / among three or more states.
Ratification
Formal confirmation by a state that it consents to be bound by a treaty it has signed.
